MidNite Solar Classic Owner's Manual (10-001-1 REV-V) — the MNGP is the Classic's display and is where the Classic's own network settings (DHCP/static, IP, subnet, gateway, DNS, web access) are configured.

transport: RJ-11 to the Classic's REMOTE jack. The MNGP is a Modbus MASTER toward the Classic, not a slave you can poll. Its existence and firmware revision are visible from the Classic side at register 4319 mngp_revision ("Also shows unit is connected"); its button presses arrive at the Classic in register 4221 RemoteButtons (Table 4221-1) and its menu state in 4220 RemoteMenuMode. gotchas: Not a device Cabin Hub would ever talk to. It is the Classic's front panel on a phone cord, and everything it shows is already available from the Classic's own registers over Ethernet. It appears in the catalogue only because it turned up as a retail SKU alongside the Classics.

It does occupy the Classic's remote bus. A driver that needs the RJ-11 RS-232 Modbus path (rather than Ethernet) will be contending with the MNGP, and the Classic's bus-forwarding flags at 4182 decide who reaches whom. Over Ethernet this is a non-issue.
Useful side effect for a driver: register 4319 being populated is a cheap way to tell whether a physical panel is attached, and 4320 mnlp_revision does the same for the Classic Lite panel.
unmappedReports: MNGP button presses (4221) and current menu screen (4220) — the panel is an input device. There is no DeviceKind for a display/keypad accessory and no MetricKind for a button event, which is correct; it is listed only so the surveyed retail SKU is accounted for.
